title: Parmesan and sage palmiers
subtitle: savoury puff pastry biscuits rolled with finely grated Parmesan and dried sage
excerpt: Parmesan and sage palmiers are savoury puff pastry twists shaped from a sheet of ready-rolled puff pastry scattered with Parmesan and dried sage, rolled from both long sides to the centre, then sliced and baked flat. The layers of pastry unfurl and caramelise around the cheese as they bake. They are crisp, flaky, and ready in under 30 minutes.
sourceNotes: Palmiers are a French pastry, the name derived from the resemblance to a palm leaf or elephant ear. Savoury versions with cheese or herbs became popular in British home baking and entertaining during the 1990s and 2000s, frequently appearing in party food collections and Delia Smith recipes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked, sliced palmiers on a flat tray. Bake from frozen at 200 degrees C, adding 3 to 5 minutes to the baking time.
recipe.batchNotes: Easy to double with an extra sheet of pastry.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sliced, unbaked palmiers keep refrigerated on a tray for up to 8 hours. Bake just before serving.

content.text: Parmesan and sage palmiers start with a sheet of puff pastry scattered with Parmesan and dried sage. Each long edge rolls inward to meet at the centre, making a double scroll. The log is sliced and baked flat; the layers puff apart around the cheese and caramelise on the underside.

Unroll the puff pastry sheet on a sheet of baking paper. Brush the entire surface lightly with beaten egg. Scatter the grated Parmesan, dried sage, and black pepper evenly over the surface, pressing the cheese down gently.
Roll one long edge of the pastry tightly toward the centre, making a compact roll. Repeat with the other long edge so both rolls meet in the middle. Press the two rolls gently together.
Refrigerate the roll for 20 minutes to firm it. Heat the oven to 200 degrees C (fan 180 degrees C / gas 6). Line two baking trays with baking paper.
Cut the roll into slices about 1 cm thick using a sharp knife. Lay each slice flat on the lined trays, spaced 4 cm apart. Brush the tops with a little beaten egg.

Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until puffed and deep golden on top. Flip each palmier over with tongs for the final 2 minutes if the underside needs more colour. Cool on a rack for 5 minutes and serve warm.

attrs.problem: Rolls unravelling in the oven and losing their palm-leaf shape
attrs.avoid: Avoid soft or warm pastry; it does not hold its shape when cut.
attrs.fix: Refrigerate the assembled roll for a full 20 minutes before slicing. Work quickly and slice cleanly with a sharp knife rather than pressing down.

attrs.problem: Cheese falling off and burning on the tray
attrs.avoid: Avoid too loose a scatter of cheese on the surface; it falls out as the pastry unrolls during baking.
attrs.fix: Press the cheese down firmly before rolling. The egg wash also helps the cheese adhere. Place a sheet of baking paper on top if the cheese is prone to flying off in the oven.
